change.devices: LordOS: you can block the camera, USB and Bluetooth for it in the Firewall.
change.files: LordOS: your home is read-only for it, except your personal folders (Documents, Downloads…); LordOS's settings, rules and launchers stay hidden.
change.network: LordOS: you can block its internet in the Firewall.
change.never: Never granted on LordOS: LordOS removes it, so part of the app may not work.
change.sound: LordOS: you can block its microphone in the Firewall.
change.talks: LordOS: cut off while a camera, microphone, USB or Bluetooth block is on for it.
change.x11: LordOS: off while its files or a device (microphone, camera, USB, Bluetooth) are blocked for it.
gone: This app is no longer in Flathub's catalog.
howItRuns: Flathub apps run inside LordOS's own view, under your Firewall, like any Linux app. What each app declares is shown above; LordOS never gives more.
look.title: Display and toolkit
display.waylandHint: Its windows are drawn directly on LordOS's Wayland.
display.waylandFallbackHint: It asks for X11 only where there is no Wayland. LordOS always gives it Wayland, so it gets no X11.
display.bothHint: It gets both and its toolkit chooses. X11 windows go through Xwayland, and X11 is off while its files or a device are blocked for it.
display.x11Hint: Only X11: LordOS shows its windows through Xwayland. While its files or a device are blocked for it, it gets no X11 and can't open windows.
display.noneHint: It asks for neither Wayland nor X11: it may have no windows.
msg.noCatalog: Flathub's catalog isn't here yet. Check your connection and try Refresh.
msg.updateAllDone: Flathub apps are up to date.
notSupported: Flathub isn't available on this computer yet: for now it is only for PCs.
perm.devicesAll: All devices: cameras, game controllers, USB
perm.failed: Couldn't read what this app declares: {reason}
perm.filesHost: All your files and the system's
perm.none: This app asks for nothing special: its own window, its own folder, the graphics card.
perm.sessionBus: Every app and service of your session
perm.title: What it declares
setup.package: Turning it on installs Flatpak, the program that runs these apps, from Debian.
setup.rules: LordOS runs them with its own rules: your Firewall applies to them, and LordOS's settings, rules and launchers stay hidden from them.
setup.title: Apps from Flathub
setup.verified: The Store shows the apps Flathub verified as published by their own developers; you can show the rest too.
setup.what: Flathub is a large catalog of Linux apps published by their developers, in Flatpak format.
showAllOff: Only apps verified by Flathub. Hidden: {count}
showAllOn: Showing every Flathub app, verified or not
subtitle: Linux apps from Flathub, run inside LordOS's own view under your Firewall.
unverified: Not verified by Flathub: the publisher may not be the app's developer.
updates.text: Installed from Flathub: {count}. Flatpak checks each one and installs what changed; an open app finishes updating when you open it again.
updates.title: Flathub apps
msg.fwBlocked: The Firewall blocks Flathub, so nothing could be downloaded. To install or update Flathub apps, allow “Flathub” in Monitor → Network.
msg.fwDenied: The Firewall blocked a connection Flathub needed ({host}). Check Flathub's rules in Monitor → Network.
msg.notRefreshed: Flathub's catalog couldn't be updated, so the last one is shown ({reason}).
settings.title: Flatpak
settings.footer: Flatpak is installed only when you turn Flathub on in the Store, and nothing of it runs in the background. Removing it takes away every Flathub app, the runtimes they used, Flathub itself and the flatpak package.
settings.showInStoreHint: Off hides the section; installed apps stay and still open.
settings.confirmDetail: {count} Flathub apps, the runtimes they used and Flathub are removed, then these packages: {packages}. You'll be asked for an administrator password.
settings.alsoData: Also move the apps' own data (~/.var/app) to the Trash
settings.removed: Flatpak was removed, with its apps and Flathub.
settings.planRefused: Flatpak can't be removed on its own: another installed package needs it. Nothing was changed.
note.obsVideos: In LordOS, OBS Studio saves recordings in your Videos folder: the other folders of your home are read-only for Flathub apps.
